4:1.sourceText: Καὶ πάλιν ἤρξατο διδάσκειν παρὰ τὴν θάλασσαν. καὶ συνάγεται πρὸς αὐτὸν ὄχλος πλεῖστος, ὥστε αὐτὸν εἰς πλοῖον ἐμβάντα καθῆσθαι ἐν τῇ θαλάσσῃ, καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος πρὸς τὴν θάλασσαν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς ἦσαν.
4:1.targetText: And again He began to teach by the sea, and there was gathered to Him a great multitude, so that He, having gone into the boat, sat in the sea, and all the multitude was near the sea, on the land,

groups.note: N1904 has historical present is gathered; LSV renders the gathering event in the past.
Greek πλεῖστος is superlative, a very great/largest multitude; LSV uses the less explicit degree a great.
Greek sitting infinitive is rendered by the finite English sat within the result clause.

4:2.sourceText: καὶ ἐδίδασκεν αὐτοὺς ἐν παραβολαῖς πολλά, καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ἐν τῇ διδαχῇ αὐτοῦ
4:2.targetText: and He taught them many things in allegories, and He said to them in His teaching:

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

4:3.sourceText: Ἀκούετε. ἰδοὺ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ σπείρων σπεῖραι.
4:3.targetText: “Listen, behold, the sower went forth to sow;

4:4.sourceText: καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ σπείρειν ὃ μὲν ἔπεσεν παρὰ τὴν ὁδόν, καὶ ἦλθεν τὰ πετεινὰ καὶ κατέφαγεν αὐτό.
4:4.targetText: and it came to pass, in the sowing, some fell by the way, and the birds of the sky came and devoured it;

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes of the sky with birds; N1904 has no corresponding sky noun or phrase here.

4:5.sourceText: καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν ἐπὶ τὸ πετρῶδες ὅπου οὐκ εἶχεν γῆν πολλήν, καὶ εὐθὺς ἐξανέτειλεν διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν βάθος γῆς·
4:5.targetText: and other fell on the rocky ground, where it did not have much earth, and immediately it sprang forth, because of having no depth of earth,

4:6.sourceText: καὶ ὅτε ἀνέτειλεν ὁ ἥλιος ἐκαυματίσθη, καὶ διὰ τὸ μὴ ἔχειν ῥίζαν ἐξηράνθη.
4:6.targetText: and the sun having risen, it was scorched, and because of having no root it withered;

groups.note: Greek when the sun rose is recast as the temporal participial phrase the sun having risen; the temporal conjunction and rising predicate share that English constituent.

4:7.sourceText: καὶ ἄλλο ἔπεσεν εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας, καὶ ἀνέβησαν αἱ ἄκανθαι καὶ συνέπνιξαν αὐτό, καὶ καρπὸν οὐκ ἔδωκεν.
4:7.targetText: and other fell toward the thorns, and the thorns came up and choked it, and it gave no fruit;

4:8.sourceText: καὶ ἄλλα ἔπεσεν εἰς τὴν γῆν τὴν καλήν, καὶ ἐδίδου καρπὸν ἀναβαίνοντα καὶ αὐξανόμενα, καὶ ἔφερεν εἰς τριάκοντα καὶ ἐν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἐν ἑκατόν.
4:8.targetText: and other fell to the good ground, and was giving fruit, coming up and increasing, and it was bearing, one thirty-fold, and one sixty, and one a hundred.”

groups.note: Greek εἰς is the yield-rate preposition with thirty, not the numeral one; the whole phrase is rendered thirty-fold.
The displayed ἐν is the preposition in, giving a sixtyfold yield with the numeral; it is not the numeral ἕν one.
The displayed ἐν plus hundred gives the yield rate, not a separate one numeral. The English a belongs to the hundred expression.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies distributive one before thirty-fold; N1904 has the yield-rate preposition εἰς, not one.
Source-witness difference: LSV has a distributive one before sixty; displayed N1904 ἐν is in, not the numeral ἕν.
Source-witness difference: LSV has a distributive one before a hundred; displayed N1904 ἐν is in, not the numeral ἕν.

4:9.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν Ὃς ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν ἀκουέτω.
4:9.targetText: And He said to them, “He who is having ears to hear—let him hear.”

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV supplies explicit recipients to them; no recipient phrase is written in this pinned N1904 verse.

4:10.sourceText: Καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο κατὰ μόνας, ἠρώτων αὐτὸν οἱ περὶ αὐτὸν σὺν τοῖς δώδεκα τὰς παραβολάς.
4:10.targetText: And when He was alone, those around Him, with the Twelve, asked Him of the allegory,

groups.note: N1904 has plural allegories as the asking object; LSV uses singular of the allegory as an English complement. The shared parable noun is linked with this number/complement difference recorded.

4:11.sourceText: καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Ὑμῖν τὸ μυστήριον δέδοται τῆς βασιλείας τοῦ Θεοῦ· ἐκείνοις δὲ τοῖς ἔξω ἐν παραβολαῖς τὰ πάντα γίνεται,
4:11.targetText: and He said to them, “To you it has been given to know the secret of the Kingdom of God, but to those who are outside, in allegories are all the things done,

groups.note: The substantivizing article before outside is expanded into an English relative who are; no separate Greek finite are is claimed.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes a knowing infinitive after given; the pinned N1904 verse has no corresponding knowing verb.

4:12.sourceText: ἵνα βλέποντες βλέπωσιν καὶ μὴ ἴδωσιν, καὶ ἀκούοντες ἀκούωσιν καὶ μὴ συνιῶσιν, μή ποτε ἐπιστρέψωσιν καὶ ἀφεθῇ αὐτοῖς.
4:12.targetText: that seeing they may see and not perceive, and hearing they may hear and not understand, lest they may turn, and the sins may be forgiven them.”

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV explicitly names the sins as forgiven; the pinned N1904 verse has an impersonal forgiveness predicate without a sins noun.

4:13.sourceText: καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς Οὐκ οἴδατε τὴν παραβολὴν ταύτην, καὶ πῶς πάσας τὰς παραβολὰς γνώσεσθε;
4:13.targetText: And He says to them, “Have you not known this allegory? And how will you know all the allegories?

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

4:14.targetText: He who is sowing sows the word;

4:15.sourceText: οὗτοι δέ εἰσιν οἱ παρὰ τὴν ὁδὸν ὅπου σπείρεται ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν εὐθὺς ἔρχεται ὁ Σατανᾶς καὶ αἴρει τὸν λόγον τὸν ἐσπαρμένον εἰς αὐτούς.
4:15.targetText: and these are they by the way where the word is sown: and whenever they may hear, Satan immediately comes, and he takes away the word that has been sown in their hearts.

groups.note: Greek into them is rendered with an English in-their-hearts construction; the relation and added hearts noun are explicitly distinguished.
N1904 has accusative them as recipient of sowing; LSV uses third-person plural possessive their with the added hearts noun. The same recipients are retained, with the grammatical recasting noted.

unmappedSource.reason: Greek article has no separate English word in this noun phrase.

unmappedTarget.reason: The LSV hearts noun is additional to N1904, which has the word sown into them without a hearts noun.

4:16.sourceText: καὶ οὗτοί εἰσιν ὁμοίως οἱ ἐπὶ τὰ πετρώδη σπειρόμενοι, οἳ ὅταν ἀκούσωσιν τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς μετὰ χαρᾶς λαμβάνουσιν αὐτόν,
4:16.targetText: And these are they, in like manner, who are sown on the rocky ground: who, whenever they may hear the word, immediately receive it with joy,

4:17.sourceText: καὶ οὐκ ἔχουσιν ῥίζαν ἐν ἑαυτοῖς ἀλλὰ πρόσκαιροί εἰσιν, εἶτα γενομένης θλίψεως ἢ διωγμοῦ διὰ τὸν λόγον εὐθὺς σκανδαλίζονται.
4:17.targetText: and have no root in themselves, but are temporary; afterward tribulation or persecution having come because of the word, immediately they are stumbled.

4:18.sourceText: καὶ ἄλλοι εἰσὶν οἱ εἰς τὰς ἀκάνθας σπειρόμενοι· οὗτοί εἰσιν οἱ τὸν λόγον ἀκούσαντες,
4:18.targetText: And these are they who are sown toward the thorns: these are they who are hearing the word,

groups.note: N1904 has an aorist heard participle; LSV renders present are hearing for the same hearing action.

unmappedSource.reason: Source-witness designation difference: N1904 has others, ἄλλοι, while LSV uses demonstrative these. Different lexical designations are not equated.

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV opens with demonstrative these where N1904 has others; these unlike words are left unpaired.

4:19.sourceText: καὶ αἱ μέριμναι τοῦ αἰῶνος καὶ ἡ ἀπάτη τοῦ πλούτου καὶ αἱ περὶ τὰ λοιπὰ ἐπιθυμίαι εἰσπορευόμεναι συνπνίγουσιν τὸν λόγον, καὶ ἄκαρπος γίνεται.
4:19.targetText: and the anxieties of this age, and the deceitfulness of the riches, and the desires concerning the other things, entering in, choke the word, and it becomes unfruitful.

groups.note: Greek of the age is rendered of this age; the shared age phrase supplies the relation while LSV adds explicit proximal determination.

4:20.sourceText: καὶ ἐκεῖνοί εἰσιν οἱ ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν τὴν καλὴν σπαρέντες, οἵτινες ἀκούουσιν τὸν λόγον καὶ παραδέχονται καὶ καρποφοροῦσιν ἐν τριάκοντα καὶ ἐν ἑξήκοντα καὶ ἐν ἑκατόν.
4:20.targetText: And these are they who on the good ground have been sown: who hear the word, and receive, and bear fruit, one thirty-fold, and one sixty, and one a hundred.”

groups.note: N1904 uses distal those, ἐκεῖνοι; LSV refers to the same final seed class with proximal these. The demonstrative-distance difference is explicit.
Greek ἐν with thirty expresses a yield rate, rendered thirty-fold; it is not a one numeral.
Greek ἐν plus sixty is a yield-rate phrase; displayed ἐν is not numeral one.
The preposition ἐν with hundred expresses the yield rate; its Greek identity is not numeral one.

unmappedTarget.reason: The LSV distributive one is additional to the pinned N1904 yield-rate phrase before thirty.
Source-witness difference: LSV has distributive one before sixty, whereas displayed N1904 ἐν is the preposition in, not numeral ἕν.
Source-witness difference: LSV has distributive one before a hundred, whereas displayed N1904 ἐν is the preposition in, not numeral ἕν.

4:21.sourceText: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς ὅτι Μήτι ἔρχεται ὁ λύχνος ἵνα ὑπὸ τὸν μόδιον τεθῇ ἢ ὑπὸ τὴν κλίνην; οὐχ ἵνα ἐπὶ τὴν λυχνίαν τεθῇ;
4:21.targetText: And He said to them, “Does the lamp come that it may be put under the measure, or under the bed—not that it may be put on the lampstand?

unmappedSource.reason: Greek ὅτι introduces direct speech and is rendered with quotation punctuation.
Greek μήτι marks a negative question expecting no; English asks Does the lamp come ...? without a separate negative word.

4:22.sourceText: οὐ γάρ ἐστιν τι κρυπτὸν, ἐὰν μὴ ἵνα φανερωθῇ· οὐδὲ ἐγένετο ἀπόκρυφον, ἀλλ’ ἵνα ἔλθῃ εἰς φανερόν.
4:22.targetText: For there is not anything hid that may not be revealed, nor was anything kept hid but that it may come to light.

groups.note: N1904 uses an except-in-order-that-it-be-revealed construction after nothing hidden. LSV recasts the same universal disclosure as no hidden thing that may not be revealed. The whole exception/purpose clause is linked; its internal Greek negation is not independently equated with an English negation of revealing.
Greek hidden/concealed adjective is rendered by the English indefinite anything kept hid; no separate kept verb is written in Greek.

4:23.sourceText: εἴ τις ἔχει ὦτα ἀκούειν, ἀκουέτω.
4:23.targetText: If any has ears to hear—let him hear.”

4:24.sourceText: Καὶ ἔλεγεν αὐτοῖς Βλέπετε τί ἀκούετε. ἐν ᾧ μέτρῳ μετρεῖτε μετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν, καὶ προστεθήσεται ὑμῖν.
4:24.targetText: And He said to them, “Take heed what you hear; in what measure you measure, it will be measured to you; and to you who hear it will be added;

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV includes a relative who hear clause in the added-to-you statement; no such clause is present in this pinned N1904 verse.

4:25.sourceText: ὃς γὰρ ἔχει, δοθήσεται αὐτῷ· καὶ ὃς οὐκ ἔχει, καὶ ὃ ἔχει ἀρθήσεται ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ.
4:25.targetText: for whoever may have, there will be given to him, and whoever has not, also that which he has will be taken from him.”

groups.note: Greek present indicative has is expressed as may have after whoever in LSV; the having predicate is shared with this mood phrasing explicit.

4:26.sourceText: Καὶ ἔλεγεν Οὕτως ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ Θεοῦ, ὡς ἄνθρωπος βάλῃ τὸν σπόρον ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς,
4:26.targetText: And He said, “Thus is the Kingdom of God: as if a man may cast the seed on the earth,

4:27.sourceText: καὶ καθεύδῃ καὶ ἐγείρηται νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν, καὶ ὁ σπόρος βλαστᾷ καὶ μηκύνηται ὡς οὐκ οἶδεν αὐτός.
4:27.targetText: and may sleep, and may rise night and day, and the seed springs up and grows, he has not known how;

4:28.sourceText: αὐτομάτη ἡ γῆ καρποφορεῖ, πρῶτον χόρτον, εἶτεν στάχυν, εἶτεν πλήρης σῖτος ἐν τῷ στάχυϊ.
4:28.targetText: for of itself the earth bears fruit, first a blade, afterward an ear, afterward full grain in the ear;

unmappedTarget.reason: LSV adds an initial for; there is no corresponding conjunction in pinned N1904 at the start of this verse.

4:29.sourceText: ὅταν δὲ παραδοῖ ὁ καρπός, εὐθὺς ἀποστέλλει τὸ δρέπανον, ὅτι παρέστηκεν ὁ θερισμός.
4:29.targetText: and whenever the fruit may yield itself, immediately he sends forth the sickle, because the harvest has come.”

groups.note: Greek παραδοῖ here describes the crop yielding itself/being ready for harvest. The reflexive English form belongs to the whole idiomatic predicate, not a separate Greek itself pronoun.

4:30.sourceText: Καὶ ἔλεγεν Πῶς ὁμοιώσωμεν τὴν βασιλείαν τοῦ Θεοῦ, ἢ ἐν τίνι αὐτὴν παραβολῇ θῶμεν;
4:30.targetText: And He said, “To what may we liken the Kingdom of God, or in what allegory may we compare it?

groups.note: Greek how may we liken is rendered To what may we liken; the comparative question and likeness predicate form one constituent.
Greek put/place in an allegory expresses the parabolic comparison, rendered may we compare. This contextual use is noted, not a general assertion that put and compare are identical lexemes.

4:31.sourceText: ὡς κόκκῳ σινάπεως, ὃς ὅταν σπαρῇ ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς, μικρότερον ὂν πάντων τῶν σπερμάτων τῶν ἐπὶ τῆς γῆς,
4:31.targetText: As a grain of mustard, which, whenever it may be sown on the earth, is less than any of the seeds that are on the earth;

groups.note: The comparative less than all the seeds is rendered less than any of the seeds; both quantify the full comparison class, with the all/any wording difference explicit.
The article introducing the on-earth modifier is expanded into the English relative clause that are.

4:32.sourceText: καὶ ὅταν σπαρῇ, ἀναβαίνει καὶ γίνεται μεῖζον πάντων τῶν λαχάνων, καὶ ποιεῖ κλάδους μεγάλους, ὥστε δύνασθαι ὑπὸ τὴν σκιὰν αὐτοῦ τὰ πετεινὰ τοῦ οὐρανοῦ κατασκηνοῖν.
4:32.targetText: and whenever it may be sown, it comes up, and becomes greater than any of the herbs, and makes great branches, so that under its shade the birds of the sky are able to rest.”

groups.note: The comparison with all the herbs is rendered greater than any of the herbs; the comparison class is shared with the all/any wording recorded.

4:33.sourceText: Καὶ τοιαύταις παραβολαῖς πολλαῖς ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς τὸν λόγον, καθὼς ἠδύναντο ἀκούειν·

4:34.sourceText: χωρὶς δὲ παραβολῆς οὐκ ἐλάλει αὐτοῖς, κατ’ ἰδίαν δὲ τοῖς ἰδίοις μαθηταῖς ἐπέλυεν πάντα.

4:35.sourceText: Καὶ λέγει αὐτοῖς ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ ὀψίας γενομένης Διέλθωμεν εἰς τὸ πέραν.
